tech_stack.architecture: Monolithic single-file REST API with MongoDB

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single static hardcoded API key shared by all callers with no principal attribution. All requests are indistinguishable — there is no way to identify which agent or service made a specific request.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication with per-caller attribution. No OAuth2 client credentials, no mTLS, no per-caller API keys, no service account definitions.
findings.recommendation: Replace the static shared API key with per-caller API keys that map to named principals, or implement OAuth2 client credentials flow with a Cognito app client or API Gateway authorizer.

blocker_remediation.immediate: Implement per-caller API keys with principal attribution via API Gateway
blocker_remediation.target_state: Each agent identity has a unique credential that is logged with every request

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: A single shared API key grants equal access to all endpoints. There is no mechanism to create scoped permissions — all callers get identical access.
findings.gap: No authorization model supporting differentiated access levels per caller identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-caller API keys with associated permission scopes at the API Gateway layer.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with usage plans and per-consumer API keys
Implement lightweight RBAC middleware

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The API key check is a binary pass/fail that grants access to all endpoints equally. No RBAC, no ABAC, no per-method checks.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to specific operations (e.g., GET only, no POST).
findings.recommendation: Implement action-level checks via API Gateway method-level authorization or route middleware.

compensating_controls: Use API Gateway with method-level authorization
Add route-level middleware checking caller permissions

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: The API key is hardcoded in source code (var API_KEY = 'ship-2013-abc123-static'). The MongoDB connection URL with internal IP is also hardcoded. No secrets management system.
findings.gap: No secrets management (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault). No credential rotation. Credentials committed to git history permanently.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials. Read from environment variables. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation.

compensating_controls: Use Kubernetes Secret (already referenced in deployment.yaml)
Rotate the exposed key immediately

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. No request logging, no principal attribution in logs, no CloudTrail, no immutable log storage. Only console.log at startup.
findings.gap: Cannot determine which caller made which request. No audit trail for forensics or compliance.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON request logging with caller attribution. Configure immutable log storage.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Read-only agents do not execute write operations, so audit logging is important but not a deployment blocker.
compensating_controls: Add structured request logging middleware
Ship logs to CloudWatch Logs with retention policy

findings.title: Cannot Suspend Individual Agent Identities
findings.description: Single shared API key means individual agent identities cannot be suspended. Revoking the key disables all callers simultaneously.
findings.gap: No ability to isolate a misbehaving agent without disrupting all other consumers.
findings.recommendation: Move to per-caller API keys managed through API Gateway with independent revocation.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with per-consumer API keys
Implement API key allowlist/blocklist

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience Patterns
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations on MongoDB connection. Each request opens a new connection with no timeout. MongoDB failures cascade to all callers.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns protect against dependency failures. Slow or unreachable MongoDB hangs requests indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Add connection timeouts, connection pooling, and circuit breaker pattern for MongoDB dependency.

compensating_controls: Configure MongoDB connection timeout options
Add connection pool with health checks

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no application-level rate limiting middleware.
findings.gap: Runaway agent loops can overwhelm the service and MongoDB at machine speed with no throttling.
findings.recommendation: Add express-rate-limit middleware or deploy API Gateway with usage plan throttling.

compensating_controls: Deploy API Gateway with rate limiting
Add express-rate-limit middleware

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, or any machine-readable API specification exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Agent frameworks cannot auto-generate tool definitions. Manual tool authoring required.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification documenting GET /rates and POST /quote.

compensating_controls: Manually author tool definitions
Generate OpenAPI spec from code annotations

findings.title: Unstructured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal objects with generic error strings. No error codes, no retryable indicators, no machine-readable categories.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured errors with error_code, message, and retryable fields.

compensating_controls: Document error responses in external error catalog
Add error classification at API Gateway layer

findings.title: No Pagination or Result Size Limits
findings.description: GET /rates returns all matching documents with no pagination, no limit parameter, and no result size cap.
findings.gap: Agents can receive unbounded result sets, exhausting LLM context windows.
findings.recommendation: Add pagination parameters (limit, offset/cursor) and enforce maximum result size.

compensating_controls: Add default limit to MongoDB queries
Agent tool definitions can specify query constraints

findings.title: No Input Validation — NoSQL Injection Risk
findings.description: No input validation. Unvalidated query params passed directly to MongoDB filter. Potential NoSQL injection vector. No type checking on POST /quote body.
findings.gap: No validation library, no schema enforcement, no structured validation errors.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation middleware (joi, express-validator). Sanitize MongoDB query inputs.

compensating_controls: Add basic type checking before queries
Deploy API Gateway with request validation

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata or Freshness Signaling
findings.description: No temporal metadata in API responses. No timestamps, no Cache-Control headers, no freshness indicators.
findings.gap: Agents cannot determine whether returned data is current or stale.
findings.recommendation: Add timestamp fields and freshness headers to responses.

compensating_controls: Add Cache-Control headers
Document expected data freshness externally

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no versioned URLs, no changelog, no breaking change detection tools.
findings.gap: API changes will break agent tool bindings silently.
findings.recommendation: Add URL versioning (/v1/rates) and create an OpenAPI specification as the contract.

compensating_controls: Pin agent tool definitions to current structure
Add URL versioning

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing (no OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray). No structured logging — only a single console.log at startup. No JSON logs, no correlation IDs.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated requests are completely unobservable.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging and X-Ray/OpenTelemetry instrumentation.

compensating_controls: Add basic request logging middleware with request_id
Instrument with X-Ray SDK

findings.title: No Alerting Configuration
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no monitoring dashboards, no anomaly detection.
findings.gap: System degradation will not be detected until agents fail.
findings.recommendation: Configure CloudWatch alarms on error rate and latency.

compensating_controls: Use Kubernetes probes as basic health monitoring
Configure CloudWatch Container Insights

findings.title: Partial Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests provide partial IaC (k8s/ directory). No Terraform/CDK for broader infrastructure. No peer review or drift detection evidence.
findings.gap: Incomplete IaC coverage. No review gates. No drift detection.
findings.recommendation: Define full infrastructure in IaC. Implement GitOps with drift detection.

compensating_controls: Enforce PR reviews on k8s/ directory
Add GitOps tooling for drift detection

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild configuration found.
findings.gap: API changes cannot be caught before deployment. No automated build, test, or deploy.
findings.recommendation: Implement CI/CD pipeline with API contract tests.

compensating_controls: Manual testing before deployment
Document expected API contract

findings.title: Zero Test Coverage
findings.description: No test files exist. No test framework in dependencies. No test scripts. Zero automated test coverage.
findings.gap: API behavior changes will not be caught by tests.
findings.recommendation: Add test framework (jest/mocha) and write API tests for both endpoints.

compensating_controls: Manual API testing via curl/Postman
Document expected API behavior

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest configuration for MongoDB. No TLS on connection. No KMS references.
findings.gap: Data potentially unencrypted at rest and in transit.
findings.recommendation: Enable TLS for MongoDB connection. Configure encryption at rest.

compensating_controls: Enable MongoDB WiredTiger encryption
Migrate to managed service with default encryption

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. No docker-compose, no environment-specific configs, no seed data.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior.
findings.recommendation: Create docker-compose for local testing and Kustomize overlays for staging.

compensating_controls: Use separate k8s namespace with test MongoDB
Create docker-compose for local testing

findings.title: Idempotency Not Applicable (Read-Only)
findings.description: No write endpoints exist. POST /quote is a stateless computation with no side effects. Idempotency is informational for read-only scope.
findings.gap: No idempotency mechanism — not needed for current read-only operations.
findings.recommendation: Implement idempotency keys if write endpoints are added in the future.

ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: Read-only agents do not execute write operations, so idempotency is informational only.

findings.title: No Rate Limit Headers
findings.description: No rate limit documentation or headers. No X-RateLimit-Remaining, no Retry-After headers in responses.
findings.gap: Agents cannot self-throttle based on quota awareness.
findings.recommendation: Include rate limit headers when rate limiting is implemented.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation (Data-Gateway)
findings.description: No identity propagation. Single API key provides no caller context. Downgraded to INFO per data-gateway archetype — serves reference data, not user-specific data.
findings.gap: No JWT, OAuth2 on-behalf-of, or user context forwarding.
findings.recommendation: Implement if service evolves to serve user-specific data.

findings.title: No Transaction Limits (Read-Only)
findings.description: No per-caller transaction limits. As a read-only service, blast radius is limited to resource consumption rather than data mutation.
findings.gap: No business-level operation caps (informational for read-only scope).
findings.recommendation: No immediate action. Implement if write operations are added.

findings.title: Business Reference Data Only — No Sensitive Data
findings.description: System stores shipping rate reference data (origin, destination, pricing). Not PII, PHI, financial records, or credentials. Stage A = No.
findings.gap: No sensitive data classification needed for current data model.
findings.recommendation: No action needed. Reassess if data model adds customer-specific or personal data.

ara_metadata.conditional_resolution: Stage A = No: not a data-handling target for sensitive data
ara_metadata.resolution_reasoning: DATA-Q1 Stage A evaluated as No — the persistent data (shipping rates) is business reference data, not PII/PHI/financial/credentials.

b1.reasoning: Stage A = No, B1 not evaluated

b2.reasoning: Stage A = No, B2 not evaluated

b3.reasoning: Stage A = No, B3 not evaluated

findings.title: No Data Quality Metrics
findings.description: No data quality metrics or monitoring for the shipping rates data.
findings.gap: No completeness monitoring, freshness SLAs, or duplicate detection.
findings.recommendation: Consider data quality monitoring for the rates collection.

findings.title: No Data Catalog or Metadata Layer
findings.description: No data catalog or metadata layer. No schema documentation for the rates collection.
findings.gap: Data model must be reverse-engineered from source code.
findings.recommendation: Document the rates collection schema in a README or schema file.

items.summary: Resolve the machine identity BLOCKER and address critical safety risks: implement per-caller authentication, secrets management, audit logging, circuit breakers, and rate limiting.
Address quality gaps: add API specification, structured errors, input validation, pagination, observability, CI/CD pipeline, and staging environment.
Polish engineering maturity: add test coverage, rate limit headers, identity propagation, and data catalog.

recommended_actions.action: Deploy centralized identity provider with per-agent credentials
recommended_actions.rationale: Single BLOCKER. Machine identity is prerequisite for all other auth controls. Recommend API Gateway with per-consumer API keys and usage plans.

recommended_actions.action: Implement secrets management and credential rotation
recommended_actions.rationale: Hardcoded credentials in source code are permanently exposed in git history. Quick win: read from environment variables already configured in k8s.

recommended_actions.action: Add structured logging and audit trail
recommended_actions.rationale: No audit trail means agent actions are untrackable. Combine with observability improvements.

recommended_actions.action: Implement resilience patterns and rate limiting
recommended_actions.rationale: Protect against cascading failures and traffic storms. Quick wins with express-rate-limit and connection timeouts.

recommended_actions.action: Create OpenAPI specification and add API versioning
recommended_actions.rationale: Enables automated tool generation for agent frameworks and prevents silent breaking changes.
